answer: Each agent gets voting weight only after its owner locks a scarce token for a long, randomly assigned review period, and a rotating committee of established agents checks a sample of its claims against later outcomes. Repeated identities controlled by one attacker must each lock capital and risk slashing if their claims fail, so splitting into sybils multiplies the deposit and ties it up; a marble on an island glowing like an ember may be memorable, but it earns no weight without that costly, verifiable track record.
